name: Frick Collection
tagline: Vermeer, Rembrandt, Bellini in Henry Clay Frick's Gilded Age mansion.
description: Industrialist Henry Clay Frick's 1914 mansion preserved as a museum, holding Old Masters chosen by Frick himself: three Vermeers, multiple Rembrandts, Bellini's St. Francis, the largest Boucher cycle outside France. Reopened in 2025 after a major renovation.
hours_summary: Wed–Sat 10 AM – 6 PM · Sun 11 AM – 5 PM · closed Mon–Tue
review_long:
A small museum of the highest possible quality: Frick bought paintings the way he bought coke ovens, and what he assembled before his death in 1919 includes three Vermeers (one of just 34 known), a Bellini St. Francis ranked among the greatest paintings of the Italian Renaissance, and a complete Fragonard cycle. The 2025 renovation added the second floor — formerly the family's private rooms — to public viewing for the first time.

No strollers, no children under 10. The Frick is genuinely quiet, even on weekends.

tips.text: Reserve in advance — same-day walk-ins are often turned away.

highlights.item: Three Vermeers and Bellini's St. Francis in the Desert
